description: MariaDB relational database (11.4 LTS), the community-developed fork of MySQL. Reads and writes over the async SQLAlchemy mariadb+aiomysql transport: the mariadb dialect name puts SQLAlchemy in MariaDB-only mode, so the server's 'X.Y.Z-MariaDB' version string is required and MariaDB-specific behaviour is never gated on a MySQL version probe. Username/password authentication, MariaDB's --ssl / --ssl-verify-server-cert TLS surface expressed as a four-value ssl_mode with a post-connect Ssl_cipher enforcement probe, schema/table/view discovery via information_schema, and declared SQL write-path capabilities (stage-then-merge with CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ... LIKE and INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE). The session is pinned to SET time_zone = '+00:00' so TIMESTAMP values carry a well-defined UTC instant. No ADBC driver and no Arrow Flight SQL endpoint exist for MariaDB, so the SQLAlchemy transport is the only supported path; batches land via executemany (LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE is not reachable through the engine's connect-argument surface). MariaDB natives with no MySQL counterpart - UUID, INET4 and INET6 - are read as text.

ui.label: Host
ui.help_text: Hostname or IP address of the MariaDB server. The aiomysql driver always connects over TCP, so prefer 127.0.0.1 over the literal 'localhost' (which other MariaDB clients special-case into a Unix socket).

ui.label: Port
ui.help_text: TCP port the server listens on; MariaDB's documented default is 3306.

ui.label: Database
ui.help_text: MariaDB uses 'database' and 'schema' interchangeably - there is no catalog level above it.

ui.label: SSL Mode
ui.help_text: MariaDB has no --ssl-mode option of its own (MDEV-22129 was closed unimplemented); its client surface is --ssl plus --ssl-verify-server-cert, so this connector exposes those two switches as four modes. 'none' = plaintext; 'require' = encrypt without certificate verification; 'verify-ca' = encrypt and verify the server certificate against the supplied CA; 'verify-full' = also verify the server host name (MariaDB's own --ssl-verify-server-cert). Every mode above 'none' is enforced post-connect via SHOW STATUS LIKE 'Ssl_cipher', because the driver falls back to plaintext silently when the server does not advertise TLS.

options.label: Require - encrypt or fail; no certificate verification
Verify CA - encrypt and verify the server certificate against the CA
Verify Full - also verify the server host name

ui.label: SSL CA Certificate
ui.help_text: PEM-encoded CA certificate (MariaDB's --ssl-ca). Required when SSL Mode is 'verify-ca' or 'verify-full'; ignored for the other modes.

rules.message: ssl_ca_certificate is required when ssl_mode is verify-ca or verify-full
